'''Adele Johanna Josiger Merritt''' is an American [[applied mathematician]] and intelligence official who served as the [[Associate Director of National Intelligence and Chief Information Officer|U.S. associate director of national intelligence and chief information officer]].

== Life ==
Merritt earned a Bachelor of Science and a Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance from [[Pace University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Chief Information Officer |url=https://www.dni.gov/index.php/who-we-are/leadership/chief-information-officer |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=www.dni.gov}}{{PD-notice}}</ref> She completed a Master of Science and Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of Rhode Island]].<ref name=":0" /> Her 1999 dissertation was titled ''Advances in Z-cyclic whist and triple whist tournaments''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis |last=Merritt |first=Adele Johanna Josiger |title=Advances in Z -cyclic whist and triple whist tournaments |date=1999 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=[[University of Rhode Island]] |oclc=48259738}}</ref> Norman Joseph Finizio was her doctoral advisor.<ref name=":1" /> Merritt was a national security fellow at the [[Harvard Kennedy School]].<ref name=":0" />

Merritt began her career at the [[National Security Agency]] as an applied research mathematician.<ref name=":0" /> In addition to holding various positions within the [[United States Intelligence Community|U.S. Intelligence Community]] (IC), she completed a joint duty assignment at the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], was the principal deputy chief information officer for cyber at the [[U.S. Department of Energy]], and served as a director and acting senior director for intelligence programs on the [[National Security Council (United States)|National Security Council]] staff during the [[Obama administration]].<ref name=":0" /> Merritt led a [[Public–private partnership|public-private partnership]] focused on addressing [[cyber threats]] to U.S. national security systems and critical infrastructure.<ref name=":0" /> Most recently, she was the program director at MISI, a non-profit focused on advancing cybersecurity innovation and collaboration through partnerships with industry, academia, and government.<ref name=":0" /> In 2022, Merritt was nominated by U.S. president [[Joe Biden]] to serve as the [[Associate Director of National Intelligence and Chief Information Officer|associate director of national intelligence and chief information officer]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Billy |date=2022-03-07 |title=Intelligence community gets new CIO in Adele Merritt |url=https://www.fedscoop.com/intelligence-community-gets-new-cio-in-adele-merritt/ |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=FedScoop |language=en}}</ref> She started in this role on January 24, 2022.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldstein |first=Phil |date=March 29, 2022 |title=Intelligence Community Gets a New CIO Amid Shifts in Cloud, Tech Architecture |url=https://fedtechmagazine.com/article/2022/03/intelligence-community-gets-new-cio-amid-shifts-cloud-tech-architecture |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=FedTech Magazine |language=en}}</ref> She resigned in December 2024 after being named CIO of the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NIH Names Adele Merritt CIO |url=https://meritalk.com/articles/nih-names-adele-merritt-cio/?_gl=1*18nrmn6*_gcl_au*MTEwMzIyNjU1Ni4xNzM0OTc4NDA5*_ga*MTE1Mzc4Mzc3OS4xNzEwNzk4ODUx*_ga_3S3PX6WJC5*MTczNjM3NjU0Ny4zOS4xLjE3MzYzNzY1NzAuMzcuMC4w |website=www.meritalk.com |access-date=8 January 2024}}</ref>

Merritt and her husband are the parents of twins.<ref name=":0" />
